messages:
sam_support: Hey team — ACME reported a recurring 401 when calling /v1/generate from their in-app WebView. User is non-technical and says "it's failing sometimes" with no visible request id in their screenshots. What is the minimal ask we can send to a non-technical contact so we can get a trace?

lina_se: Ask for three things only: 1) a screenshot of the browser/network panel showing the failed request, 2) the exact time (including timezone) they saw the error, and 3) a tiny curl we can run (we can give them a one-liner to copy/paste). Keep wording non-technical.

jess_eng: +1. Provide them this curl snippet with placeholders and say "paste this into Terminal / PowerShell and send the output". Make sure to include the Authorization header masked. Example we can paste:```bash
curl -v "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"input":"test trace"}'
```

mike_mobile: For WebView specifically: tell them to check the in-app console (if they can open devtools / remote debug) and look for headers named like `x-rd-request-id` or `x-redwood-trace` or `session-ref`. If they can't do devtools, ask them to forward the screenshot of the network request where the response code and headers are visible.

sam_support: How do we phrase the non-technical ask?

lina_se: Short copy you can DM: "Hi — sorry about the error. Could you do two quick things so we can track this down? 1) Take a screenshot of the screen where you see the error and, if possible, the browser's network/console tab showing the failed request. 2) Open Settings → Help → Send Feedback (or the app menu) and paste this one-line command we give you. We'll only use it to reproduce the failure. Thanks!"

jess_eng: Add a pre-filled command for Windows/mac non-admin users (PowerShell friendly):```powershell
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' -Headers @{'Authorization'='Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>'; 'Content-Type'='application/json'} -Method Post -Body '{"input":"test trace"}'
```

mike_mobile: If they absolutely can't run curl/ps: ask for a screenshot of the error time + the device local time shown on the status bar. We can correlate logs server-side by timestamp and approximate client IP. Also ask whether they were on cellular, office VPN, or corporate proxy — proxies often strip headers.

lina_se: Important: tell them to send the exact time in ISO-ish format, e.g., "2025-11-03 14:23 UTC" or "11/03/2025 9:23AM PST" — we need timezone.

sam_support: Any quick troubleshooting steps we can ask them to try before escalating?

jess_eng: Ask them to retry with a new request and copy any error message text. If they can edit headers (advanced users) tell them to add `X-Trace-Request: test-<shortid>` and include that value in the message to us. We'll search for that value in logs.

infra_bot: Automated hint: If you provide `X-Trace-Request` we will correlate within 90s by default. If missing, search window expands to +/- 5m. See https://infra.redwood/help/traces (internal). :gear:

mike_mobile: For Android/iOS embedded SDKs: if using the SDK, the client-only request id lives in the SDK logs under `session.hash` or `req_ref`. Ask them to take a screenshot of the app's "Diagnostics" or "About -> Logs" screen (if the app surfaces it).

sam_support: Great — I'll send a short DM template and curl/powershell snippets. Also will add a fallback: "If you can't do any of the above, please reply with the exact local time and a screenshot of the error". Thanks. :thumbsup:

lina_se: One more: mention corporate proxies in the DM: "If you are on a company network, try reproducing from your phone's cellular data and send the result" — that often proves proxy header stripping.

jess_eng: And remind them to redact their API key when pasting output — we only need headers and the `x-rd-request-id` value or the entire network request details (with key replaced by <REDACTED>).

sam_support: Sending now. I'll follow up with the trace id once we have it.
